name: agent-guide-test-anchor-removed
body:
source: spine-backfill/feedback-3 on solution.component.agent-guide. Inconsistency: agent-guide carried `implemented-by -> go.github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide/internal/scaffold.TestAgentGuidesMatchFormat`, a test function in internal/scaffold/agentsguide_test.go. No production component anchors test code, and this edge had been added only to give requirements.requirement.agent-guide-drift-check a path to code (see requirements.note.spine-agent-guide-drift-check). Resolution [autonomous]: removed the implemented-by edge to the test function. No drives hop needed fixing and no test anchor was re-added, because agent-guide already owns the production code the drift check protects: internal/scaffold/libraryguide.go (File) and the seed/writer functions scaffold.Init, scaffold.InitExternal, scaffold.InitLibrary and scaffold.writeHelloSeed. The requirement still reaches that code through its existing drives: agent-guide-drift-check -> domain.group.authoring and domain.group.templating (both realised-by solution.component.agent-guide) and, via templating, template-registry and renderer. Verification on this branch: the requirement-spine query (Requirement ->Drives-> Domain ->RealisedBy-> Solution ->SpecImplementedBy-> code) yields 17 distinct production code units for agent-guide-drift-check and 0 rows for the violation query (requirements reaching no code, and requirements reaching only test code). agent-guide's implemented-by set was then 5 production anchors: internal/scaffold/libraryguide.go, scaffold.Init, scaffold.InitExternal, scaffold.InitLibrary, scaffold.writeHelloSeed; the TestAgentGuidesMatchFormat edge is gone.

UPDATE [with user] (section-helpers reconciliation, final-review feedback-11): the final traceability review asked agent-guide to also anchor the two embedded guide sources, so implemented-by edges to internal/scaffold/seed/AGENTS.md and internal/scaffold/libraryguide/AGENTS.md were added; for the same review an edge to the drift-test file internal/scaffold/agentsguide_test.go was added too, and requirements.note.feedback-11-load-time-traceability briefly claimed to supersede this note. The user ruled that the no-production-component-anchors-test-code rule STANDS, so the drift-test edge was removed and the supersession is withdrawn (see requirements.note.feedback-11-load-time-traceability). agent-guide's implemented-by set is now 7 production anchors: the original five — internal/scaffold/libraryguide.go, scaffold.Init, scaffold.InitExternal, scaffold.InitLibrary, scaffold.writeHelloSeed — plus the two AGENTS.md guide files internal/scaffold/seed/AGENTS.md and internal/scaffold/libraryguide/AGENTS.md. internal/scaffold/agentsguide_test.go is not anchored.

UPDATE (2026-09-30, boy-scout pass before merge; test-harness scope) [with user]: the rule is scoped to PRODUCTION components. A test-harness/CI component may anchor its own test files, so solution.component.native-e2e-ci's implemented-by -> e2e/native_test.go (e2e.TestNativeRelease) and solution.component.anonymous-install-e2e's implemented-by -> e2e/install_test.go (e2e.TestAnonymousPackageInstall) are consistent and stay; neither is a production component (native-e2e-ci is realised by domain.service.publish-release, anonymous-install-e2e by domain.service.install-kalide, and their bodies define them as the e2e tests themselves). agent-guide is a production component, so its removed test anchor stays removed. Full decision: requirements.note.test-harness-test-code-anchors. Open question (not changed): .github/workflows/native-e2e.yml exists as an unowned workflow File node and could additionally anchor native-e2e-ci.
